## Project Overview

The goal of this project is to examine the relationship between the geographic patterns of school segregation and how this overlaps with juvenile and young-adult involvement within the criminal legal system. The project will have a specific focus on Mecklenburg County in North Carolina. I plan to first investigate how the racial and socioeconomic geographic disbursement of Mecklenburg County has changed over time. Using this information, I want to then look at how school boundaries have been drawn and adjusted over time creating this environment of school segregation (particularly following the end of court-ordered busing). I will then look to see how this correlates to juvenile criminal legal system activity as well as general school characteristics (school budget, attendance, graduation rates, student and teacher demographic, and suspension/expulsion rates). I hope to identify patterns in how school and neighborhood geography may be connected to how young people throughout Mecklenburg County interact with the criminal legal system.
